plotting_plan.title: Overview of the Economics-Informed Machine Learning (EIML) Architecture
plotting_plan.objective: Conceptual architectural diagram illustrating the 4 Corporate Finance Pillars (Liquidity, Solvency, Profitability, Efficiency), the Point-in-Time Forensic Filter, the Dual-Stream EINN with Differential Monotonicity Regularization (R_mono), Altman Double-Deficit Boundary Penalty (R_bound), and Positive-Cone Weight Projection.

plotting_plan.title: Corporate Distress Trajectory Across Four Macroeconomic Crisis Regimes (2008-2022)
plotting_plan.objective: Time-series dual-line and shaded-regime bar chart showing annual distress rates (%) from 2008->2009 to 2021->2022, highlighting the 2011-2012 Banking NPL Crisis peak (15.21%) and the 2020-2022 COVID-19 & Corporate Bond Crisis peak (15.77%), alongside Purged Train/Val/Test split boundaries.

plotting_plan.title: Accuracy vs. Economic Consistency Score (ECS) Pareto Frontier on Out-of-Time Crisis Test Set
plotting_plan.objective: 2D scatter and Pareto frontier plot comparing Classical Models (Altman Z'', Ohlson O, Logistic Regression), Black-Box ML (SVM, Random Forest, Unconstrained GBDT, Deep MLP), and Proposed EIML (Mono-GBDT, EINN) across PR-AUC (x-axis) and Economic Consistency Score ECS % (y-axis).

plotting_plan.title: Ceteris-Paribus Response Curves: Black-Box Hallucinations vs. EINN Monotonicity
plotting_plan.objective: Side-by-side sensitivity response curves showing predicted distress probability P(Distress) as a function of ShortDebt/Debt and Operating ICR, contrasting the non-monotonic oscillations of Unconstrained MLP against the strictly monotonic trajectories of EINN.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Corporate financial distress and shadow credit risk in emerging markets have escalated sharply during recent macroeconomic and corporate bond liquidity crises, requiring early-warning models that are both highly accurate out-of-time and strictly compliant with economic solvency laws.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Classical parametric models (Altman Z''-Score, Ohlson O-Score) obey economic signs but fail to capture nonlinear interactions, whereas black-box ML models (XGBoost, Deep MLP) exhibit severe monotonicity violations (42.18%-88.10%) and degrade under out-of-distribution crisis shifts, compounded by pervasive look-ahead and survivorship biases in emerging-market panel studies.
search_directions: Foundational papers on corporate bankruptcy and financial distress prediction (Altman 1968, Ohlson 1980, Shumway 2001, Campbell Hilscher Szilagyi 2008)
Machine learning benchmarks for corporate bankruptcy and credit risk prediction (Barboza Kimura Altman 2017 Expert Systems with Applications)
Monotonicity constraints, physics-informed neural networks, and shape-constrained machine learning in finance and credit scoring

related_work_strategy.overview: Synthesize three methodological clusters to establish the necessity of combining forensic point-in-time panel hygiene with monotonic and boundary-constrained representation learning.

content_bullets: State the trade-off between classical solvency theory and black-box ML hallucinations (42.18%-88.10% monotonicity violations).
Introduce the EIML framework (Mono-GBDT and EINN) with partial monotonicity and Altman boundary constraints.
Summarize the 15-year Vietnamese corporate panel (2008-2022, 720 firms), forensic data cleaning, zero-look-ahead purged split, and SOTA out-of-time results (0.7894 and 0.9597 AUC-ROC, 100% ECS).
